mostWorthwhile.text: Making the mineral-rich sea brought the weathering sequence together: rainfall altered continental rock, and rivers carried material to the sea. It made the world feel connected.

leastWorthwhile.text: The successive checks of rainfall, rivers, the vent and crust were frustrating dead ends, especially because their descriptions suggested plausible connections to minerals.

surprise.text: Earth and water made pigment rather than minerals for the sea. The mention that it had no painter yet was an intriguing hook for a living world.

arbitrary.text: Rainfall could weather a continent but had no available combination with stone crust. That distinction felt more like a recipe constraint than an explained physical difference.

continue.text: Yes. The pigment's suggestion of a future painter and the connected geological processes make me curious about what the world could make next, though I would hope for fewer dead-end checks.
